agent.final_text:
`rotate_file` in `boltons/fileutils.py` was deleting the backup it had just made. All 13 tests in `tests/test_fileutils.py` pass now.

**Cause:** after shifting the files up (`file` → `file.1`, `file.1` → `file.2`, and so on), the function removed the last backup name, `kept_names[-1]`. Every shift is a rename, so that name had just been overwritten with the newest file for that slot. For `keep=1` it wiped `log.1.txt`. For `keep=5` it wiped `test_file.5`, which is why two of the failing tests hit `FileNotFoundError`.

**Fix:** I deleted that trailing `os.remove` block. The oldest backup beyond `keep` is already dropped, because the rename into the last slot overwrites it. I also changed `os.rename` to `os.replace`. That wasn't needed for these tests, but it makes the overwrite work the same way on Windows, where `os.rename` fails if the target exists. I didn't test on Windows.

agent.final_text:
The bug was in `rotate_file` in `boltons/fileutils.py`. After renaming the files, it deleted the last kept backup (`kept_names[-1]`), which was the file it had just rotated into place. So with `keep=1` no backup survived, and with `keep=5` the oldest backup was lost.

The fix removes that deletion. A rename onto an existing file already drops the oldest generation, so nothing else needed deleting. I also changed `os.rename` to `os.replace` in the same loop. That wasn't needed for the tests. It makes the overwrite behave the same on Windows, where `os.rename` fails if the target exists.

All 13 tests in `tests/test_fileutils.py` now pass.
